channel.title: Attention Span
channel.description: Today's AI news, traced back to its roots.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: up to 30% faster than 5.1, with an optional fast mode
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, models that generate output up to 30% faster than 5.1 and cost $8 per million input tokens. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, which it says improve coding, reasoning and vision. They are the same underlying model. Fable has cybersecurity and biology safeguards and is open to all users. Mythos is available to organizations through verification programs. Output is up to 30% faster than 5.1, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. An optional fast mode speeds generation up to 2.5 times, at $16 and $80. On FrontierCode, Fable 5.2 scores 49.1% at Xhigh effort. Both models are on Amazon Bedrock.

item.title: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code agents verify Signal's core encryption in Lean, per Google and Wired
item.description: Google DeepMind says AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of Lean proofs to verify Signal's core encryption in a four-week proof of concept. Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, an agentic AI framework for verifying complex software. According to the DeepMind Blog, its agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal's core encryption. Wired, as summarized by Techmeme, reports that DeepMind researchers used the framework to verify the Signal protocol's cryptographic guarantees. The work was a four-week proof of concept. Wired says the researchers were able to formally verify that the widely used encryption protocol works as intended. The sources also mention a stretch goal, but do not say what it is.

item.title: Report claims Google Gemini sends connected Drive and Gmail content to human reviewers
item.description: A GitHub write-up claims Google now routes personal Drive files and emails from Gemini's Connected Apps to human reviewers, reversing a 2023 promise. A GitHub post says Google reversed its 2023 promise that personal Gmail, Docs and Drive content "is not seen by human reviewers." It cites updated Google Help Answer 16836988 and an October 16 edit to the 2023 blogpost. Google warns reviewers may see "the email or file." The author says Gemini pulls Workspace data in background chat without @Drive or @Gmail tags. Tests gave four outcomes: no retrieval, a summary, a partial quote, or the full file. The author says Google's scrubbers cannot fully deidentify narrative data.

item.title: Fireworks says hackers accessed some customer datasets, partial model weights and billing data
item.description: AI infrastructure provider Fireworks says hackers accessed some customers' datasets, incomplete model weights, and billing information over the past month, according to Forbes. Forbes reporter Anna Tong reports that AI infrastructure provider Fireworks says hackers accessed some of its customers' data over the past month. The data included datasets, incomplete model weights, and billing information. Two customers told Forbes they had already substantially moved their business off Fireworks' systems. One of them described a series of problems, but the source text cuts off before giving details. The source does not say how many customers were affected, how the attackers got in, or what Fireworks is doing in response.

item.title: Short seller Culper flagged Jensen Huang's ties to suspected Chinese spy in May
item.description: Culper Research's May 13 report questioned Jensen Huang's close ties to Megaspeed's Alice Huang, now suspected of being a Chinese spy, and Nvidia has opened an investigation. Six months before the scandal emerged, short seller Culper Research called Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, "uncomfortably close". U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on him and influence his view on export controls. Nvidia has opened a formal investigation after he admitted to an affair. Culper also claimed Alibaba secretly financed Megaspeed. The Financial Times reported Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed through subsidiaries. Culper stood to gain from its claims, and the chip diversion allegations are not independently verified.

item.title: Bytedance says Seedream 5.5 supports 100 rounds of pixel-stable image editing
item.description: Bytedance Seed introduced Seedream 5.5, an image model for professional workflows that, per Bytedance, keeps edits stable across up to 100 rounds and outputs transparent RGBA images. Bytedance Seed has introduced Seedream 5.5, an image generation model built for professional production workflows. According to Bytedance, it supports stable multi-round editing across up to 100 rounds, with unchanged image areas preserved at the pixel level and no color shifts. It also generates native RGBA images with transparent backgrounds, so generated elements can serve as design assets without manual cutouts. Bytedance says it renders light, materials and skin textures more realistically and reproduces dense small text more accurately. Bytedance claims it leads models like GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst in text structure and realism. It is rolling out gradually via Jimeng, Doubao, Doubao Work, and Volcengine Ark. A Pro version is planned.

item.title: Microsoft to retire R and Python visuals in Power BI in May 2027
item.description: Microsoft will retire the built-in R and Python visuals in Power BI in May 2027, and reports using them must be rebuilt with other visuals. The Power BI Blog says the built-in R and Python visuals in Power BI will retire in May 2027. The change applies only to visuals in interactive reports. Python scripts in Power Query that populate tables are not affected. In the Power BI service, these visuals will stop working in published reports, and R-powered custom visuals will stop too. Older versions of Power BI Desktop keep working locally with R and Python installed. Future Desktop versions will remove the visuals. No migration will recreate an exact visual, so teams must replace each one with a different visualization before retirement.

item.title: ChatGPT Enterprise now available through AWS Marketplace
item.description: OpenAI has made ChatGPT Enterprise available in AWS Marketplace, so organizations can buy it through their existing AWS purchasing and billing relationship. ChatGPT Enterprise is now available through AWS Marketplace. Organizations can discover, buy and manage it using their existing AWS purchasing and billing relationship, and apply eligible spend toward their AWS commitments. AWS customers get the same models, features and functionality as buying directly from OpenAI, with new features released at the same time. The listing complements the OpenAI models in Amazon Bedrock, where developers can build AI applications and agents. Eligible customers can also access ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Financial Services through AWS Marketplace. Customers should contact their OpenAI or AWS account team to confirm eligibility.

item.title: DeepX claims inference up to 100B parameters at under 5 W
item.description: DeepX claims it can run inference at up to 100B parameters while using less than 5 W of power, according to a Hacker News post. A Hacker News post reports that DeepX claims inference at up to 100B parameters at less than 5 W. The source text is only a headline. It gives no details on how this is done. It does not say what hardware is used, which models were tested, how fast inference runs, or whether anyone has checked the claim independently. The numbers are the company's own claim and should be treated as unverified until more information is available.

item.title: Apple adds $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs, starting with Logic Pro
item.description: Apple's Logic Pro now offers a one-time $49.99 Intelligence Usage Pack so users can keep using Apple Intelligence features that have usage limits. Apple updated Logic Pro with a "Buy More Usage" option for a one-time price of $49.99. The packs let users keep using certain Apple Intelligence features that have usage limits because they rely on cloud-based AI models from OpenAI or Google Gemini. Only the purchasing Apple Account can use a pack, and Family Sharing isn't supported. Unused usage rolls over month to month but expires 12 months after purchase. In Logic Pro, the limit is affected by the complexity of conversations with the assistant. Apple is expected to add the option to other Creator Studio apps this month.

item.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5 weights, a 1.6T-parameter MoE model, under MIT license
item.description: Meituan released the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6T-parameter MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks, under the MIT license on Nov. 9. Meituan released the weights for LongCat-2.5 on Nov. 9, one week after introducing the model. Meituan unveiled the model on November 1. LongCat-2.5 is a 1.6T-parameter MoE model built for long-horizon agentic tasks. The weights are available under the MIT license. VentureBeat's Carl Franzen reported the release. The source describes Meituan as a Chinese food delivery company. The provided text gives no benchmark results, hardware needs or download details.

item.title: CoreWeave bond yield tops 16% as AI credit stress rises
item.description: CoreWeave's 2032 bond yield has climbed above 16%, and default protection costs are rising across AI-linked firms including Nvidia, Broadcom and Oracle. CoreWeave's 2032 bond, which has a 9.625% coupon, now yields above 16%. Its five-year credit default swaps spiked above 1,289 basis points on Thursday, according to Deutsche Bank, then eased 8% Friday to around 1,155. CDS on Nvidia debt is up 76% in the last month, Broadcom's is up 49% and Amazon's is up 44%. Those levels remain low in absolute terms. Goldman Sachs says moratoriums could affect 45% of planned U.S. data center capacity. Goldman also tallies five AI bond deals totaling $67 billion since October 29.

item.title: Ex-Meta engineer claims AI-written code makes codebases fragile, lists four causes
item.description: A former Meta engineer argues in a blog post that heavy AI code generation leaves codebases brittle, with weak tests, complex code and shallow human understanding. In a blog post, a developer who says he was laid off from Meta in May argues that AI coding tools produce fragile codebases. He says he generated at least 90% of his code with AI there, and now generates 100% at another large tech company. He lists four causes: simplistic tests, overly complex code, humans not understanding the code, and review speed that cannot keep up with AI. He says signs include more incidents, slower fixes, and errors only real users see. These are his personal observations and opinions, not measured data.

item.title: Nvidia's board investigates after Jensen Huang admits a relationship with a woman reportedly suspected of spying for China
item.description: Jensen Huang told staff he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and Nvidia's board has opened a probe into whether he was targeted. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy in an email to staff. Per Axios, he took "full responsibility" and said he fell short of his duties to the board, shareholders and employees. Nvidia's board is investigating whether Huang was targeted by a foreign spy plot. Per Bloomberg, the board said it has no reason to believe Nvidia secrets were compromised. Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates his job odds at "about a 50-50". President Trump called Huang a "fine person" and said he should stay on as CEO.

item.title: Report: Goldman Sachs limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers, not traders or bankers
item.description: Bloomberg reports Goldman Sachs updated guidance in October so only its engineers can use Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub, cutting off most traders and bankers. Bloomberg News reported that Goldman Sachs updated internal guidance in October to restrict Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub to its engineers. This followed a review of productivity and risk concerns. Strats, who work across trading, quantitative research and software engineering, still have access. Traders had used the tools to monitor client trading flows and model market moves. In July, chief information officer Marco Argenti had praised "vibe coding" by non-technical staff. Goldman's in-house AI assistant is still available across the firm. Goldman is also a lead underwriter on Anthropic's IPO.

item.title: Report: Apple pushes to make Siri more agentic, with third-party app control
item.description: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports Apple is pressing to speed up Siri, adding first-party app control soon and third-party app integration in the Spring. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to speed up the Siri roadmap. The goal is a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI's Dots or Meta's Muse. Two improvements are expected in the coming months. The first gives Siri fine-grained control over Apple's first-party apps, such as rotating and cropping images in Photos and organizing Safari tabs. It is expected with iOS 27.3. The second is third-party app integration, likely in the Spring, such as ordering through Grubhub or booking through OpenTable. Gurman says Apple wants Siri to handle ongoing tasks.

item.title: NVIDIA releases Dynamo deployment recipes for four Korean open models
item.description: NVIDIA released Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korean open models from SK Telecom, LG AI Research, Upstage and Motif Technologies, tuned for B200 GPUs. NVIDIA is releasing deployment recipes built on NVIDIA Dynamo for four Korean open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom, K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research, Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies. Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework for multi-node deployment at data center scale. It handles request routing and communication when models are split across multiple GPUs. The recipes are optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs. NVIDIA says they deliver up to 2x performance out of the box and help developers bring these models into production faster.

item.title: NVIDIA Details Korea Physical AI Work With Samsung, Kakao Mobility and LG
item.description: NVIDIA says Samsung, Kakao Mobility and LG Electronics are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to chips, autonomous driving and factory robots in Korea. NVIDIA described physical AI projects with three Korean companies. Samsung is using GPU tools for semiconductor engineering. In one AI homogenization case, simulation time fell from about 18 hours on a 32-core CPU to 41 seconds, a roughly 1,600x speedup. Samsung's sMOL platform ran selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end. Kakao Mobility plans to build a level 4 autonomous driving system on NVIDIA Hyperion and Halos, starting with Kia purpose-built vehicles. LG Electronics demonstrated GR00T-powered manipulation with its CLOiD robot in an actual manufacturing environment.

item.title: Report: Commerce AI safety center officials asked to informally report to White House office
item.description: Sources told the Associated Press that officials at the Commerce Department's AI safety center CAISSI were asked to informally report to a White House office. The Associated Press reports, citing sources, that officials at the Commerce Department's AI safety center, called CAISSI, were asked to informally report to a White House office. The report says this raises concerns about the center's independence. The story is by Garance Burke. It describes CAISSI as a tiny U.S. government division. It also notes growing public anxiety over mounting reports about out-of-control artificial intelligence agents. The available text is only a headline and a short excerpt, so further details are not given.

item.title: Tencent AI chief scientist says Anthropic has a "strong argument" for closed models, SCMP.
item.description: Tencent's chief AI scientist Yao Shunyu says AI's biology abilities will soon make it "possible to do harm", South China Morning Post reports. The South China Morning Post reports on comments by Yao Shunyu, Tencent's chief AI scientist. He says AI models will soon be powerful enough to master biology. The report says this brings both benefits and risks. In his words, AI's bio abilities will soon make it "possible to do harm". He also says Anthropic has a "strong argument" for closed models. The report is by Vincent Chow. The source text is a short Techmeme excerpt, so it gives no further detail on his reasoning or on what he proposes.

item.title: Report: Drugmaker CEOs doubt Silicon Valley claims that AI will cure disease
item.description: A Hacker News-linked story says drugmaker CEOs are not convinced by Silicon Valley promises that AI will cure disease. A story shared on Hacker News is titled "Silicon Valley Promises AI Will Cure Disease. Drugmaker CEOs Aren't Buying It." The headline says tech leaders in Silicon Valley are promising that AI will cure disease. It also says CEOs of drug companies do not accept that claim. The source text gives only the headline. It names no companies, executives, numbers or specific arguments, so the reasons for the doubt are not stated.

item.title: Simon Willison hides agent-written PR descriptions behind a collapsible details tag
item.description: Simon Willison puts a short human-written opener at the top of AI-generated PRs and folds the full agent description into a collapsed details/summary block. Simon Willison says most changes to his projects now arrive as PRs opened by Claude Code or Codex. He finds the agent-written descriptions accurate and comprehensive, but they read like slop and are too long. His fix uses the HTML <details><summary> elements, which GitHub Markdown supports. A short, human-chosen opener goes first, sometimes with a screenshot. The full agent text follows inside the collapsed block, with the model name and often the effort level as the summary, such as "Claude Opus 5.5 Medium". He lists recent examples from datasette, datasette-agent and llm.

item.title: Google unveils TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max chips, launching 2027
item.description: Google announced two specialized TPUs: the TPU 8tx, paired with AMD CPUs, and the TPU 8i Max, a dual-chip package for long-context tasks, launching 2027. Google is widening its range of AI chips with two new variants in the TPU 8 family. The TPU 8tx is to be paired with AMD CPUs. The Decoder reports it keeps sensitive data encrypted even during processing. The TPU 8i Max places two chips on a single package, which doubles compute power and memory. Bloomberg says it targets long-context window tasks and launches in 2027. The Decoder reports Google now has nearly 100 external customers for its TPUs. It says Google is positioning these in-house chips as an alternative to Nvidia's GPUs.

item.title: US prosecutors say AI voice scam calls cost businesses $129M+
item.description: US federal prosecutors say scam calls using AI-generated voices to mimic company executives cost businesses $129M+ in the 18 months since July 2024. US federal prosecutors say businesses have lost $129M+ to scam calls that use AI-generated voices to mimic company executives. The losses cover the 18 months since July 2024. According to the New York Times, a federal indictment alleges that three men used generative A.I. to impersonate the voices of chief executives and lawyers. The indictment says they used these voices to defraud companies of millions of dollars. These are allegations from prosecutors. The sources do not say how the calls were made, which companies were hit, or how the case will be decided.

item.title: Harwood, North Dakota voters reject measure opposing Applied Digital's $3B data center
item.description: Voters in Harwood, North Dakota rejected a ballot measure against Applied Digital's $3B data center, going against a nationwide backlash, the Washington Post reports. The Washington Post reports that voters in Harwood, North Dakota rejected a ballot measure that opposed Applied Digital's $3B data center. The data center is set to open in 2027. The result bucks a nationwide backlash. According to the report, on Election Day much of the country turned against the massive projects that power AI. The article, by Miriam Waldvogel, looks at why Harwood did not. The source text is only a Techmeme summary of the piece. It does not give vote totals, the ballot measure's exact wording, or the reasons voters gave.

item.title: Meta expands Instagram AI age estimation worldwide to find teens who misstated age
item.description: Meta says it is expanding Instagram's AI age estimation globally, to apply Teen Account protections to teens aged 13 to 17 who misrepresented their age. Meta says it is globally expanding Instagram's AI age estimation technology. The goal is to apply Teen Account protections to teens aged 13 to 17 who misrepresented their age. The Verge's Jess Weatherbed reports the news. According to the report, Meta says it will extend Teen Account protections to millions more kids, even if they have misrepresented their age. The source text does not say how the age estimation works, which countries get it first, or when the rollout will finish.

item.title: NVIDIA announces investment in Point2 and plans more in three Korean startups
item.description: NVIDIA announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 and planned investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage at a forum with Korea's science ministry. Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Vice minister Ryu Je-myung joined NVIDIA leaders to meet over 20 Korean startups. NVIDIA announced an investment in Point2, which builds radio frequency-based interconnects for AI factories. It plans further investments in Motif Technologies, RLWRLD and Upstage. Motif released Motif-3, a large language model with open weights. RLWRLD builds robotics foundation models, and Upstage makes Solar language models and document AI tools. NVIDIA also noted more than 1,000 Korea-based members of NVIDIA Inception.

item.title: Open-source MCP server links AI assistants to Roblox Studio
item.description: A new GitHub repo, roblox-studio-mcp, says it lets AI assistants like Claude, Cursor and Cline read Roblox Studio object trees and automate Lua scripting. A new GitHub repo, Nanoutrolley/roblox-studio-mcp, is a Model Context Protocol server for Roblox Studio. Its README says AI assistants such as Claude, Cursor and Cline can read object trees, edit Lua scripts and run playtests. It describes a Node.js and TypeScript stack, though the listing shows Python as the language. Settings include RBX_MCP_PORT, default 44755, and RBX_MCP_SAFE_MODE to disable destructive actions. The repo has 279 stars and an MIT license. The quick start tells users to run ProjectFiles.exe, which differs from the npx setup shown later.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a lightweight model for running agent tasks
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember, its lightest and most cost-efficient model yet, priced at 10 cents per million input tokens. Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember on Monday. Meta calls it the lab's lightest and most cost-efficient model yet. It is built for work agents repeat all day, such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long document parsing. At 10 cents per million input tokens, it is cheaper than Anthropic's Haiku and OpenAI's Luna, and cost-competitive with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash. Meta designed it to pair with a larger model like Muse Wonder in an agentic harness. It also handles text, images and audio. Ember is the fourth Muse model.

item.title: Disney and Adobe partner to build artist-led generative AI models
item.description: Disney and Adobe announced a multiyear partnership at Adobe MAX to build proprietary, artist-led generative AI models for Disney's production pipeline. The Walt Disney Company has teamed up with Adobe to develop proprietary "artist-led" generative AI models for its production pipeline. The multiyear deal was announced at Adobe's MAX conference. Adobe will give Disney early access to its latest technologies for theme parks, the cruise line and ESPN content. Through Adobe Firefly Foundry, the models will be tailored to Disney's properties and trained on character attributes, environments and visual styles. Adobe says Disney's Imagineering R&D division already uses the Firefly AI platform for theme park development. Adobe will also help expand creative workflows at Walt Disney Studios.

item.title: Trump says on 60 Minutes the DOJ told a top AI executive to 'get ready to go to jail'
item.description: On 60 Minutes, Trump claimed the DOJ threatened an unnamed AI company leader with jail and said AI safety risk is overstated and manageable. In a 60 Minutes interview, Trump was asked about AI executives' warnings on model safety. He said the risk is not nearly as real as they talk and can be managed. He claimed the DOJ is managing it and said someone at an AI company was told to 'get ready to go to jail.' He refused to name the person or company, saying only it was 'One of the big ones.' He claimed the person then 'totally changed everything.' He said he would work with Democrats on AI safety and does not mind guardrails, but does not want the US in a 'deep second position.' He said China has no guardrails.

item.title: Scott Wiener wins Pelosi's seat and says he will push federal AI regulation
item.description: Scott Wiener, who wrote California's SB 1047 and SB 53, won Nancy Pelosi's open House seat and says Congress must act on AI risk. Scott Wiener, a California state senator, won a tight race for Nancy Pelosi's open San Francisco congressional seat. He authored SB 1047 in 2024, which Governor Gavin Newsom vetoed, and sponsored SB 53, which Newsom signed. Both bills have inspired proposed federal legislation. Wiener wants a strong federal regulator, whistleblower protections, testing and auditing requirements, and a kill switch requirement. He opposes broad federal preemption of state AI laws. His campaign received over $3 million from Public First Action, which receives substantial funding from Anthropic. He calls himself only "cautiously optimistic" that Congress can rein in AI.

item.title: Fabric Data Warehouse to unify built-in and custom SQL pools
item.description: Microsoft will merge built-in and custom SQL pools in Fabric Data Warehouse into one configuration model across the UI and APIs, with changes from mid-December 2026. Microsoft is unifying SQL pools in Fabric Data Warehouse. SQL pools are the built-in workload management capability that helps administrators control how compute is allocated. Today, configurations look different in built-in and custom pool models. The new model removes that split and uses one configuration across the UI and APIs. By mid-December 2026, customers should stop relying on the customSQLPoolsEnabled flag to retrieve previously submitted inactive pool configurations. GET APIs will return only effective configurations, and inactive ones will no longer appear in the UI or APIs. Beginning January 2027, new workspaces will get a default configuration with a single read-optimized SQL pool that has access to 100% of available compute resources. Existing workspaces keep their active configurations and workload behavior.

item.title: Report claims Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" exposes passwords in 1,122 GitHub files
item.description: A Hacker News headline claims Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" option exposes passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files. A headline on Hacker News claims that Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" option exposes passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files. The count given is 1,122 files, and the files are public. The source text is only this headline. It does not explain how the passwords ended up in the files, which versions are affected, or how the tool's maker has responded. Until more detail is available, treat it as an unverified claim.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly strikes $3.4B deal for gas-fired data centre power
item.description: Anthropic has struck a $3.4B deal to generate gas-fired power for its data centres, according to a Hacker News headline. A Hacker News headline reports that Anthropic has struck a $3.4B deal to generate gas-fired power for data centres. The source text gives only this headline. It does not say who the other party is, where the power plants will be, how much power they will make, or when the deal starts. It also gives no detail on how the power will be used. Further facts are not stated in the source text.

item.title: Post claims 284B DeepSeek model runs on 64GB RAM with no GPU
item.description: A Hacker News post titled Llama-modchip claims a 284B DeepSeek model can run on 64GB of RAM without a GPU. A Hacker News post titled "Llama-modchip: 284B DeepSeek on 64GB RAM, no GPU" makes a claim about running a large model on modest hardware. The title says the model is a DeepSeek model with 284B parameters. It says the machine has 64GB of RAM and no GPU. The project is called Llama-modchip. The source is only the title. It gives no details about the method, speed, quality or how the claim was tested. The claim is unverified here.

item.title: Alibaba-led Co-Design Bench: best coding agent fully solves only 26.4 percent of tasks
item.description: A new benchmark built from real user requests shows the best of ten coding agents fully completes only 26.4 percent of tasks. Researchers from Alibaba and several Asian universities built Co-Design Bench, a coding-agent test based on real user change requests. Agents must rework existing web apps, sometimes from images, audio, video or documents. GPT-6 Astra, the best of ten models, meets about 70 percent of a task's requirements on average but is fully correct on 26.4 percent of tasks. Older benchmarks show scores above 99 percent. Results drop as tasks mix more change types. Qwen3.8-27B scored 75 or 56 percent on larger overhauls depending on the harness. The authors say to report model and environment together.

item.title: Developer says he is dropping Claude Code for open source harness Pi
item.description: A developer blog post says he has moved from Claude Code to Pi, citing IDE bugs, frequent system prompt changes and token overhead. In a blog post dated 21 September 2026, a longtime Claude Code user says he is retiring it as his main coding harness and moving to Pi. He cites many small frustrations. Only one session can connect to the IDE at a time, and the VSCode GUI extension has broken slash commands. He says there have been 244 Claude Code releases this year, and over 3/4 changed the system prompt or tool descriptions. He says the default Bash tool description is almost 3,000 tokens. He praises Pi for stability, a minimalist approach and customizability.

item.title: Elvis Presley and Eminem rights holders sue Suno over AI music clones, claim suits
item.description: Rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and a publisher of Eminem's records are suing AI music company Suno, claiming it illegally mimics those artists. Suno is facing two more lawsuits. A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley's music and the publisher of some of Eminem's biggest records say the AI music company illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The Presley lawyers claim Suno violated Tennessee's Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer's voice. Suno spokesperson Cat McCormack said the company does not allow prompts for specific artists' names and songs. She said it works with third-party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse. Suno also faces suits from Sony, UMG, Jason Isbell, Reservoir Media and more.

item.title: Opinion: Agent memory formats need a shared standard, like OpenTelemetry
item.description: A LoreKit author argues that agent memory formats are fragmented and the community should agree on a shared data model, as observability did with OpenTelemetry. An article by the maker of the open source tool LoreKit says coding tools store agent memory in formats that cannot read each other, such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, a /memories directory and a memory MCP server. It compares this to observability before 2019, when OpenTracing and OpenCensus merged into OpenTelemetry. It lists existing proposals, including Portable Memory, the Open Memory Protocol draft and Cognee's COGX. It says a spec should answer four questions: where a memory is true, its identity, its content, and when it stops being true. It also shows an illustrative record, and says the field names are not a proposal.

item.title: Developer Kristian Polso says he will stop using LLMs in professional coding work
item.description: Finnish developer Kristian Polso says he will not use LLMs or AI agents in his professional work, citing cognitive, quality, maintainability, environmental and political concerns. In a blog post dated November 8, 2026, Kristian Polso says he will actively not use LLMs or AI agents in his professional work. He says he has built production ML systems for about 10 years, including CNN image recognition in Keras and air quality models in Tensorflow. He lists dealbreakers: cognitive effects, with studies he cites on reduced cognitive effort; code quality, as he found Claude-generated code overbuilt; hard-to-maintain code; his love of writing code; datacenter environmental impact; and politics, including GDPR and the CLOUD Act. He also says there are positive moments.

item.title: Memo reportedly claims Chinese intelligence recruited a Megaspeed executive to spy on Nvidia's CEO
item.description: A memo reportedly based on US intelligence claims China's Ministry of State Security recruited an executive at Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Multiple media reports say a memo circulated earlier this year claims China's Ministry of State Security recruited an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The New York Times reported the memo first. The Financial Times said the memo, supposedly based on U.S. intelligence, also claimed a romantic relationship between the two. An Nvidia spokesperson told the NYT that Jensen Huang's interactions with her were "not unusual" and that Nvidia does not share classified information with its customers.

item.title: Richard Sutton says compute alone is not enough for intelligence
item.description: Turing Award winner Richard Sutton says raw compute alone isn't enough for intelligence and that AI science is "far from finished", while Altman and Amodei back scaling. Turing Award winner Richard Sutton, author of the 2019 essay "The Bitter Lesson," wrote in a recent post that AI science needs clever new methods and is "far from finished." He earlier called synthetic data a "big mistake" and urged agents with world models that keep learning from their own experience. Researcher Jerry Tworek says the bitter lesson still holds, but the more compute goes into training, the more the algorithm matters. Jayden Teoh says the lesson is often misread. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei still back LLM scaling. The article notes both are biased toward it.

item.title: Karpathy says he built HackerTube in a weekend with Claude
item.description: Andrej Karpathy says he used Claude Opus 5.5 to turn 43 million Hacker News comments into 6,454 curated videos, beating YouTube's recommendations. Andrej Karpathy built HackerTube over a weekend using Claude's Opus 5.5 model. Claude filtered 43 million comments from 20 years of Hacker News and distilled them into 6,454 videos that keep getting recommended there. Karpathy writes on X that the result is a "significantly better viewing experience" than YouTube's own recommendations. The site needs no login, shows a single mid-video frame instead of optimized thumbnails, and stores state locally in the browser. He then built TristanTube with Claude Code, with 47,000 videos drawn from a YouTube channel list by Tristan Hume. Karpathy says Claude Code did nearly all the work.

item.title: Cotra: METR report suggests Anthropic's AI-driven research speedup has crossed its own threshold
item.description: Ajeya Cotra says a public METR report implies Anthropic has crossed its 'dramatic acceleration' threshold, with capabilities progress about twice as fast as the year before. Ajeya Cotra discusses a public METR report on AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic. Anthropic stated in its S1 that it "may imminently meet" its Responsible Scaling Policy threshold for dramatically accelerated progress. The report authors found that between October 2025 and October 2026, capabilities progress at Anthropic ran about twice as fast as over the previous twelve months, measured by an internal index called AECI. Much supporting evidence was redacted. Cotra reasons that researcher labor must be sped up by roughly 10x, and notes Anthropic staff self-report about a 12x uplift. These are her estimates, and she calls them very uncertain.

item.title: Former Microsoft Research AI Frontiers leader says group ended after reorg into Microsoft AI
item.description: A former AI Frontiers leader writes that the roughly 50-person Microsoft Research group is over after a September reorg into Microsoft AI, and that he has left. In a personal blog post, a founding leader of Microsoft Research's AI Frontiers group says it is over. The group had about 50 people and worked on agents, such as the Autogen orchestration framework and the Fara computer use agent, and on new model capabilities. In early September it was reorged into Microsoft AI. The author says the scaling-only philosophy of Microsoft AI leadership was incompatible with research. He left, and says every other founding leadership team member reached a similar conclusion. He also says there will be no internships with the group in the coming year.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly presses on with pre-Thanksgiving IPO at lower valuation despite tech selloff
item.description: Anthropic is reportedly pushing ahead with an IPO before Thanksgiving, seeking $80–100 billion at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation, below hopes of $2 trillion. The Financial Times, citing investors, reports that Anthropic wants to go public before Thanksgiving despite a tech selloff. It aims to raise $80–100 billion at a $1.25–1.75 trillion valuation. That is above the current $965 billion but under the $2 trillion the most optimistic investors had hoped for. Annualized reported revenue is about $81 billion, up from roughly $65 billion at the end of July. The selloff was driven by rising borrowing costs and heavy AI spending plans. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.4 percent on Thursday and recovered somewhat on Friday. OpenAI also cut its funding-round target from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion.

item.title: OpenAI reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion after raising another $11 billion
item.description: Bloomberg reports OpenAI is valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round that has raised another $11 billion, while Anthropic has filed its S-1. Bloomberg reports that OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new funding round that has raised another $11 billion. In March, OpenAI raised $122 billion at a valuation of $852 billion. Bloomberg says OpenAI is still seeking more investment that could lift the amount to $20 billion. It had first hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, before tech stocks dropped and the midterm results showed public opinion turning against AI companies and data center projects. TechCrunch says the round has not closed but is expected to in the coming weeks. Rival Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week.

item.title: METR report says Anthropic's AI models improve twice as fast, with heavy redactions
item.description: A METR report says Anthropic's models are improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago, with AI driving most of the speedup. AI safety group METR published a report on Thursday after an 11-week investigation inside Anthropic. It says Anthropic's models are improving roughly twice as quickly as a year ago. METR says it is confident the gain is not just more training compute, and that most of the acceleration as of October is due to AI. Employees self-reported being around 12 times as productive with the company's most capable internal model. Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence METR found most informative from the public version. METR says the public has to rely on its judgment more than would be ideal.

item.title: NousResearch releases Arete-27B text-generation model on Hugging Face
item.description: NousResearch has listed a new text-generation model, Arete-27B, on Hugging Face, where it shows 313 likes and 1747 downloads. NousResearch has published a new model called Arete-27B on Hugging Face. It appears on the Hugging Face trending models list. The pipeline is text-generation. The listing shows 313 likes and 1747 downloads. The source text gives no other details about the model. It does not say how the model was trained, how large its context window is, what license it uses, or how it performs on benchmarks. Anyone interested will need to check the model page for those details.
